correctness.rationale: Independently recomputed every one of the 3^15 labelled states at each threshold, without executing frozen scripts. checks/petersen_images.py computes the successor of each resting edge from disjoint active incidences at its two Petersen endpoints; the other phases have their unconditional successors. Iterated images of the complete state set are nested and stabilize precisely on the periodic set. Traversing this set gives each orbit once; successive synchronous predecessor layers give exact first entry and inherit the orbit label. For all four thresholds the attractor/period/basin populations, entry histogram, joint time and period histogram, and individual basin-size histogram match both frozen output tables in full. The four recorded max depths are 12,6,3,3; directly checked 94238 at depth 12, and 66495→5626834→12602018→3228168→169→2→0 with exact depths 6 through 0. All-rest is fixed and the only fixed state since phases 1 and 2 always change. The threshold-one period lcm is 120, giving equality after 12 and failure one update earlier. Run python3 checks/petersen_images.py with theta=1,2,3,4 as the positional argument (NumPy); each checks/petersen_images_*.out is saved. This certifies the stated finite graph and thresholds only.

evidence: Triangle-locking classifies all recurrent states at the rounded half-degree threshold on connected graphs with every vertex triangular; the only non-rest ones are balanced proper three-colorings rotating in period three.
The strict-density theorem requires ρ(G)<theta, while the whole four-regular graph attains ρ=2. Doba and Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff address structural asymptotics of threshold one.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Triangle-locking directly applies since at each base vertex the incident Petersen edges make a triangle in its connected line graph. Combined with the Tait obstruction it eliminates all periodic non-rest states, not just period three. It does not bound the transient by six or count basins. The strict-density result does not apply at theta=2.
